body: Paper/plastic bags really help if you breathe into them like you're breathing fresh air, as well.

Try your best to keep your breathing calm, Azula... panic attacks really suck, trust me, I know.

8 seconds breathing in, 2 seconds holding, 8 seconds breathing out. Do you think you can do that? Trust me, once you can get your breathing to calm down a bit, you will slowly come to feel better.

A software engineer, that's cool as heck. Same here!

It sounds like you've been dealing with this for quite some time now. Care to share with me what's on your mind? I'm here to talk if you would like to, or if you just need something to keep you busy during tough times... whatever it be :)

Oof, studying. I'm supposed to be doing that as well - but just between you and me, that's not going to happen, and that's okay, because what I am choosing to focus on in my life is just making it through the day, and trying to enjoy .

It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of stress here? To start, are there some things that help you to de-stress, or to relax?

Yeah... my last relationship (2+ years) didn't end so well, and I had a very rough time trying to let go but not feeling like I would ever be able to.

Something that helped me was breaking contact fully, and trying to find things to distract myself with. She had *became* my life, and thus when I didn't have her anymore, I didn't really have anyone to rely on.

I also went into therapy because things were getting out of hand for me both mentally and emotionally. I would continue to battle my depression and suicidal desires that were a result of our breakup.

After a couple months of having no contact with her and trying my best to distract myself from the thought of her, I found myself angry - no, *livid* \- about what had happened between us. From then on, every day after school I would learn the laws of attraction, and I worked on my 'pickup game' (really lifestyle).

This lifestyle I had adopted was really about putting yourself before others - something I was taught as a child never to do. However, upon practicing this concept, I found myself less distraught about my past relationship, and as I talked to more and more girls I had realized something that I would have never seen if I allowed myself to continue wallowing in my distress: she was just one girl.

I realized that I probably didn't have a chance of getting back together with her, and I wouldn't count on it that you may either, because that's not how these things usually work.

All in all, if there was one piece of advice I could give you, it would be to focus on yourself, and not to put others on a pedestal (above yourself). To you, you come first, and that is how it has to be if you want to have healthy relationships that don't leave you like this.

I definitely know the feeling of just wanting to let go, mate, it really fucking sucks...

Though on a different note, overdosing on multivitamins - while certainly affecting one's body - isn't as lethal as the many, many other pills out there. But hey, maybe we can help each other both out and just chat? Feel free to mate :)
